The 2022 NFL draft featured record-setting draft results for the Georgia Bulldogs, the reigning College Football Playoff national champions. Georgia had 15 players selected in the NFL draft, eclipsing the previous modern-era record of 14 picks, which was set by Ohio State in the 2004 NFL Draft and later tied by LSU in 2020. The Bulldogs have five defensive players selected in the first round from a unit that allowed a national-best 10.2 points per game last season.

Georgia alone was responsible for nearly a quarter of the Southeastern Conference's 65 selections, which tied a record the SEC set in 2021.

Here's a complete breakdown of the number of draft picks by school and by conference.

The 2022 NFL draft featured record-setting draft results for the Georgia Bulldogs, the reigning College Football Playoff national champions. Georgia had 15 players selected in the NFL draft, eclipsing the previous modern-era record of 14 picks, which was set by Ohio State in the 2004 NFL Draft and later tied by LSU in 2020. The Bulldogs have five defensive players selected in the first round from a unit that allowed a national-best 10.2 points per game last season.

Georgia alone was responsible for nearly a quarter of the Southeastern Conference's 65 selections, which tied a record the SEC set in 2021.

*   For the 14th time in the last 15 years, the SEC once again tied or led the nation in First Round NFL Draft selections, as the league produced 15 opening-round draft picks.
*   The 15 selections in the opening round tied for the most in the history of the NFL Draft (set by the SEC in 2020).
*   This is the fifth time in the last six years, and seventh in the last nine, the SEC has produced 10 or more First Round selections.
*   During the last 21 NFL Drafts, the SEC has a nation-leading 194 players taken in the opening round, an average of over nine per season.
*   The SEC had six of the first 15 selections and nine of the first 20 of the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   The SEC now has 170 First Round NFL Draft selections since 2010.
*   Since 2010, the SEC has nearly double (170) the total amount of First Round selections than the next closest conference (Big Ten – 88).
*   Nine different SEC teams had a player taken in the First Round of the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   The SEC now has 61 Top 10 picks since 2009 and 67 since 2007.
*   Since 2009, Top 10 NFL picks by league: 
    *   SEC (61)
    *   Big 12 (28)
    *   B1G (28)
    *   ACC (27)
    *   Notre Dame (5)
    *   AAC (3)
    *   MAC (3)
    *   BYU (2)
    *   Mountain West (1)

*   Georgia and Texas led the SEC with three First Round selections in the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   Alabama has a First-Round selection in each of the past 17 NFL Drafts, the longest streak in SEC and college football history, as well as the most First Round picks nationally since 2007 with 49.

*   For the 14th time in the last 15 years, the SEC once again tied or led the nation in First Round NFL Draft selections, as the league produced 15 opening-round draft picks.
*   The 15 selections in the opening round tied for the most in the history of the NFL Draft (set by the SEC in 2020).
*   This is the fifth time in the last six years, and seventh in the last nine, the SEC has produced 10 or more First Round selections.
*   During the last 21 NFL Drafts, the SEC has a nation-leading 194 players taken in the opening round, an average of over nine per season.
*   The SEC had six of the first 15 selections and nine of the first 20 of the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   The SEC now has 170 First Round NFL Draft selections since 2010.
*   Since 2010, the SEC has nearly double (170) the total amount of First Round selections than the next closest conference (Big Ten – 88).
*   Nine different SEC teams had a player taken in the First Round of the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   The SEC now has 61 Top 10 picks since 2009 and 67 since 2007.
*   Since 2009, Top 10 NFL picks by league: 
    *   SEC (61)
    *   Big 12 (28)
    *   B1G (28)
    *   ACC (27)
    *   Notre Dame (5)
    *   AAC (3)
    *   MAC (3)
    *   BYU (2)
    *   Mountain West (1)

*   Georgia and Texas led the SEC with three First Round selections in the 2025 NFL Draft.
*   Alabama has a First-Round selection in each of the past 17 NFL Drafts, the longest streak in SEC and college football history, as well as the most First Round picks nationally since 2007 with 49.

The SEC once again was the conference with the most players taken in the NFL draft. And a lot of the SEC players chosen in 2022 were from either Georgia or LSU.

Sixty-five SEC players were taken over the seven rounds of the draft. And 25 of those players were either Bulldogs or Tigers. The SEC's number of draftees ties the record it set in 2021 when 65 players were picked a year ago.

[Georgia set a modern draft record with 15 selections](https://sports.yahoo.com/georgia-sets-nfl-record-players-selected-2022-draft-214308406.html) over the seven rounds of the draft.[Five Georgia defenders were taken in the first round](https://sports.yahoo.com/2022-nfl-draft-georgia-sets-record-with-five-defenders-picked-in-first-round-040058804.html) on Thursday night and 10 more players — including punter Jake Camarda — were taken over the other six rounds.

LSU was a semi-surprising second among SEC teams with a host of selections across the final four rounds of the draft. Six LSU players were selected on Saturday after cornerbacks Derek Stingley and Cordale Flott were two of the team's four selections on the first two days of the draft. LSU also had a specialist chosen in the draft; [kicker Cade York went in the fourth round to the Cleveland Browns.](https://sports.yahoo.com/browns-take-a-kicker-in-4th-round-highest-for-a-kicker-since-roberto-aguayo-in-2016-172227706.html)

Seven Alabama players were chosen in the draft and six of those seven were taken in the first three rounds. Alabama had two players chosen in each of the first three rounds and cornerback Jalyn Armour-Davis was the last Crimson Tide player selected when the Ravens took him at No. 119.

The Big Ten was again second among all conferences with 48 draftees. Penn State led the conference with eight players taken. And yes, that number includes a punter. Jordan Stout went in the fourth round to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/teams/baltimore/).

Six Ohio State players were drafted and Michigan and Wisconsin each had five players drafted.

The Big 12 tied with the Pac-12 for the third-most draftees with 25 and the ACC had 21 players taken. The Big 12 could have been all alone in third had a Texas player been taken in the draft. None of the conference's 25 selections were from Texas. It was the first time since 2014 that a Longhorn hadn't been taken in the draft.

The AAC was tops among non-Power Five conferences with 19 draftees and 37 players were taken in the draft from schools outside of the top level of college football. [You can click here for a full list of all 262 draftees.](https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/draft/)

The SEC once again was the conference with the most players taken in the NFL draft. And a lot of the SEC players chosen in 2022 were from either Georgia or LSU.

Sixty-five SEC players were taken over the seven rounds of the draft. And 25 of those players were either Bulldogs or Tigers. The SEC's number of draftees ties the record it set in 2021 when 65 players were picked a year ago.

[Georgia set a modern draft record with 15 selections](https://sports.yahoo.com/georgia-sets-nfl-record-players-selected-2022-draft-214308406.html) over the seven rounds of the draft.[Five Georgia defenders were taken in the first round](https://sports.yahoo.com/2022-nfl-draft-georgia-sets-record-with-five-defenders-picked-in-first-round-040058804.html) on Thursday night and 10 more players — including punter Jake Camarda — were taken over the other six rounds.

LSU was a semi-surprising second among SEC teams with a host of selections across the final four rounds of the draft. Six LSU players were selected on Saturday after cornerbacks Derek Stingley and Cordale Flott were two of the team's four selections on the first two days of the draft. LSU also had a specialist chosen in the draft; [kicker Cade York went in the fourth round to the Cleveland Browns.](https://sports.yahoo.com/browns-take-a-kicker-in-4th-round-highest-for-a-kicker-since-roberto-aguayo-in-2016-172227706.html)

Seven Alabama players were chosen in the draft and six of those seven were taken in the first three rounds. Alabama had two players chosen in each of the first three rounds and cornerback Jalyn Armour-Davis was the last Crimson Tide player selected when the Ravens took him at No. 119.

The Big Ten was again second among all conferences with 48 draftees. Penn State led the conference with eight players taken. And yes, that number includes a punter. Jordan Stout went in the fourth round to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/teams/baltimore/).

Six Ohio State players were drafted and Michigan and Wisconsin each had five players drafted.

The Big 12 tied with the Pac-12 for the third-most draftees with 25 and the ACC had 21 players taken. The Big 12 could have been all alone in third had a Texas player been taken in the draft. None of the conference's 25 selections were from Texas. It was the first time since 2014 that a Longhorn hadn't been taken in the draft.

The AAC was tops among non-Power Five conferences with 19 draftees and 37 players were taken in the draft from schools outside of the top level of college football. [You can click here for a full list of all 262 draftees.](https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/draft/)

## Pre-Draft Analysis

Walker is an EDGE defender with an excellent combination of height, bulk, length and straight-line speed. His pass rush is built on strength and explosion. If he can develop smoother counter moves and unlock his potential as a pass-rusher, he'll improve his sack numbers. As a run defender, Walker is a strong tackler with the long arms to lock out and locate the ball. He also has great versatility, as he lined up at defensive end 298 times, defensive tackle 184 times and linebacker 93 times in 2021, according to ESPN Stats & Information. _-- Steve Muench_  
  
**Matt Miller's NFL comp:** Kwity Paye

## Post-Draft Analysis

Walker's versatility makes him an excellent fit for first-year coordinator Mike Caldwell's multiple front defense. His upside as a pass-rusher should give the Jaguars' rush a much-needed boost. His ability to line up anywhere along the defensive front and drop on passing downs will make it easier for Caldwell to mask from where he's bringing pressure and who is dropping into coverage. It'll also help Caldwell create favorable pass rush matchups. Jacksonville's defense was tied for 27th in sacks last season (32 sacks) despite blitzing at the fifth-highest rate in NFL and needed someone to complement 2019 first round pick Josh Allen. _-- Muench_  
  
**Projected Year 1 impact:** Day 1 starter. With Josh Allen as the team's only feared edge rusher, Travon Walker steps into a situation where he can contribute from day one and likely can be a double digit sack type of player right away from multiple spots. _-- Jordan Reid_

## Pre-Draft Analysis

Walker is an EDGE defender with an excellent combination of height, bulk, length and straight-line speed. His pass rush is built on strength and explosion. If he can develop smoother counter moves and unlock his potential as a pass-rusher, he'll improve his sack numbers. As a run defender, Walker is a strong tackler with the long arms to lock out and locate the ball. He also has great versatility, as he lined up at defensive end 298 times, defensive tackle 184 times and linebacker 93 times in 2021, according to ESPN Stats & Information. _-- Steve Muench_  
  
**Matt Miller's NFL comp:** Kwity Paye

## Post-Draft Analysis

Walker's versatility makes him an excellent fit for first-year coordinator Mike Caldwell's multiple front defense. His upside as a pass-rusher should give the Jaguars' rush a much-needed boost. His ability to line up anywhere along the defensive front and drop on passing downs will make it easier for Caldwell to mask from where he's bringing pressure and who is dropping into coverage. It'll also help Caldwell create favorable pass rush matchups. Jacksonville's defense was tied for 27th in sacks last season (32 sacks) despite blitzing at the fifth-highest rate in NFL and needed someone to complement 2019 first round pick Josh Allen. _-- Muench_  
  
**Projected Year 1 impact:** Day 1 starter. With Josh Allen as the team's only feared edge rusher, Travon Walker steps into a situation where he can contribute from day one and likely can be a double digit sack type of player right away from multiple spots. _-- Jordan Reid_

# 2022 NFL Draft picks by college team, school: Georgia defense sets first-round record, SEC dominates again

## Georgia and the SEC led the way among the schools and conferences represented Thursday night

[![Image 189: David Cobb ](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2020/01/27/927cdfbb-c58c-42f7-b2cd-b6028d112ebe/thumbnail/80x80/20c71c6e361e25a5a509826e42528def/david-cobb.png)](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/david-cobb/)

 By [David Cobb](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/david-cobb/)

 Apr 29, 2022  at 12:07 am ET • 2 min read 

[Add CBS Sports on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbssports.com)

![Image 190: jordandaviscbs.jpg](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/2021/09/16/7f28ab91-7e96-4feb-9513-98a359166857/jordandaviscbs.jpg?crop=16:9&width=560&quality=85&format=webp)

USATSI

Georgia made history in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft on Thursday night when the Bulldogs had five defensive players from their national championship team selected in the first round. It marks the first time a college team has seen that many players from its defensive unit taken among the top 32 picks in a draft.

Consider that no other entire program had more than two players selected in Round 1, and Georgia's achievement is even more impressive. In fact, the Dawgs had more defenders selected than the ACC, Pac-12, AAC respectively had total picks.

Highlighting UGA's haul on Thursday was No. 1 overall pick Travon Walker, a defensive end who went to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Following Walker's selection, a bit of collegiate diversity ensued as five of the first six picks came from different conferences. But by night's end, the opening round featured a familiar flavor as 12 of the 32 picks came from SEC schools.

Georgia led the way its five overall selections: No. 13 pick Jordan Davis (Eagles), No. 22 pick Quay Walker (Packers) and No. 28 pick Devonte Wyatt (Packers) and No. 32 pick Lewis Cine (Vikings) joined Travon Walker in the festivities. All five played key roles in helping Georgia win a national title this past season, and they likely won't be the last defensive players selected from an all-time great Georgia defense as the draft continues Friday and Saturday. In fact, many were surprised Nakobe Dean was not among the first 32 picks, but he should be off the board early in Round 2.

The SEC once again led the way with 12 first-round picks, the same number of players it had chosen last year. In fact, the Big Ten also repeated its second-place finish with seven first-round picks, again mirroring its number of selections from a year ago. The Big Ten's haul was headlined by No. 2 pick Aiden Hutchinson, a defensive end from Michigan.

From a collegiate perspective, there was another bit of history on Thursday night. Alabama [tied Miami's record](https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2022-nfl-draft-alabama-ties-miami-for-college-football-record-with-first-rounder-in-14th-straight-draft/) of 14 straight drafts with at least one first-round selection as offensive lineman Evan Neal (No. 7 to the Giants) and receiver Jameson Williams (No. 12 to the Lions) each went in the first round. The Crimson Tide are on pace to break that record in 2023.

Here's 2022 NFL Draft broken down by school at the conclusion of the first round.

## 2022 NFL Draft picks by schools, conferences

### SEC (12)

*   [Georgia](https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/teams/UGA/georgia-bulldogs/)— 5
*   Alabama — 2
*   LSU — 1
*   Mississippi State — 1
*   Texas A&M — 1
*   Arkansas — 1
*   Florida — 1

# 2022 NFL Draft picks by college team, school: Georgia defense sets first-round record, SEC dominates again

## Georgia and the SEC led the way among the schools and conferences represented Thursday night

[![Image 189: David Cobb ](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/r/2020/01/27/927cdfbb-c58c-42f7-b2cd-b6028d112ebe/thumbnail/80x80/20c71c6e361e25a5a509826e42528def/david-cobb.png)](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/david-cobb/)

 By [David Cobb](https://www.cbssports.com/writers/david-cobb/)

 Apr 29, 2022  at 12:07 am ET • 2 min read 

[Add CBS Sports on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbssports.com)

![Image 190: jordandaviscbs.jpg](https://sportshub.cbsistatic.com/i/2021/09/16/7f28ab91-7e96-4feb-9513-98a359166857/jordandaviscbs.jpg?crop=16:9&width=560&quality=85&format=webp)

USATSI

Georgia made history in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft on Thursday night when the Bulldogs had five defensive players from their national championship team selected in the first round. It marks the first time a college team has seen that many players from its defensive unit taken among the top 32 picks in a draft.

Consider that no other entire program had more than two players selected in Round 1, and Georgia's achievement is even more impressive. In fact, the Dawgs had more defenders selected than the ACC, Pac-12, AAC respectively had total picks.

Highlighting UGA's haul on Thursday was No. 1 overall pick Travon Walker, a defensive end who went to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Following Walker's selection, a bit of collegiate diversity ensued as five of the first six picks came from different conferences. But by night's end, the opening round featured a familiar flavor as 12 of the 32 picks came from SEC schools.

Georgia led the way its five overall selections: No. 13 pick Jordan Davis (Eagles), No. 22 pick Quay Walker (Packers) and No. 28 pick Devonte Wyatt (Packers) and No. 32 pick Lewis Cine (Vikings) joined Travon Walker in the festivities. All five played key roles in helping Georgia win a national title this past season, and they likely won't be the last defensive players selected from an all-time great Georgia defense as the draft continues Friday and Saturday. In fact, many were surprised Nakobe Dean was not among the first 32 picks, but he should be off the board early in Round 2.

The SEC once again led the way with 12 first-round picks, the same number of players it had chosen last year. In fact, the Big Ten also repeated its second-place finish with seven first-round picks, again mirroring its number of selections from a year ago. The Big Ten's haul was headlined by No. 2 pick Aiden Hutchinson, a defensive end from Michigan.

From a collegiate perspective, there was another bit of history on Thursday night. Alabama [tied Miami's record](https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2022-nfl-draft-alabama-ties-miami-for-college-football-record-with-first-rounder-in-14th-straight-draft/) of 14 straight drafts with at least one first-round selection as offensive lineman Evan Neal (No. 7 to the Giants) and receiver Jameson Williams (No. 12 to the Lions) each went in the first round. The Crimson Tide are on pace to break that record in 2023.

Here's 2022 NFL Draft broken down by school at the conclusion of the first round.

The **2022 NFL draft** was the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League")'s 87th annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_draft "NFL draft") and was held from April 28–30, 2022, at the [Caesars Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Forum "Caesars Forum") on the [Las Vegas Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Strip "Las Vegas Strip") in [Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada") next to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). The first round was held on Thursday, April 28, and was followed by the second and third rounds on Friday, April 29. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on Saturday, April 30. It was the first draft to be held in the [Las Vegas metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_metropolitan_area "Las Vegas metropolitan area") and the state of [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada").

The first five selections were defensive players, the second-most taken at the start of a draft after the six in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_NFL_draft "1991 NFL draft"). Along with the [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_NFL_draft "1972 NFL draft") and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_NFL_draft "2000 NFL draft") drafts, it marked the third time defensive players were the first two picks after the first three picks in the previous year's draft were quarterbacks. Five [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_football "Georgia Bulldogs football") defensive players were taken during the first round, the most from an individual school in a draft. In addition to the high number of defensive selections, nine offensive linemen were taken in the first round, the most since [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NFL_draft "2013 NFL draft"). Conversely, only one quarterback was selected in the first round at 20th overall, the lowest for a draft's first quarterback since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_NFL_draft "1997 NFL draft"), and no running backs were taken in the first round for the first time since [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NFL_draft "2014 NFL draft").

A record nine draft-day trades with first-round picks were made, which resulted in less than half of the first-round selections being made by the teams that initially owned them. Analysts attributed the high number of trades to eight teams entering the draft without a first-round selection and a general absence of highly touted prospects.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-1)

## Host city

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city")]

Las Vegas was originally scheduled to host the [2020 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft "2020 NFL draft"), coinciding with the [Oakland Raiders' relocation to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders_relocation_to_Las_Vegas "Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas"). Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") the draft was held as a [virtual event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_event "Virtual event"). Las Vegas was given the 2022 Draft as a result.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-2)

Draft activities were held around two main locations on the Las Vegas Strip; invited players walked a floating [red carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_carpet "Red carpet") on the man-made lake in front of the [Bellagio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_(resort) "Bellagio (resort)") and its [fountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountains_of_Bellagio "Fountains of Bellagio"). The plans were similar to those originally intended for the 2020 draft, although a plan for players to be transported onto the stage by boat was scrapped in favor of using walkways.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)

Caesars Forum housed infrastructure for the event.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)[The Linq Promenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Linq_Promenade "The Linq Promenade") hosted the NFL Draft Experience, which featured fan activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4) Parts of [Flamingo Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo_Road_(Las_Vegas) "Flamingo Road (Las Vegas)") and [Las Vegas Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Boulevard "Las Vegas Boulevard") were closed to vehicle traffic to allow spectators to travel between the two sites.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

The **2022 NFL draft** was the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League")'s 87th annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_draft "NFL draft") and was held from April 28–30, 2022, at the [Caesars Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Forum "Caesars Forum") on the [Las Vegas Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Strip "Las Vegas Strip") in [Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada") next to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). The first round was held on Thursday, April 28, and was followed by the second and third rounds on Friday, April 29. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on Saturday, April 30. It was the first draft to be held in the [Las Vegas metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_metropolitan_area "Las Vegas metropolitan area") and the state of [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada").

The first five selections were defensive players, the second-most taken at the start of a draft after the six in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_NFL_draft "1991 NFL draft"). Along with the [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_NFL_draft "1972 NFL draft") and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_NFL_draft "2000 NFL draft") drafts, it marked the third time defensive players were the first two picks after the first three picks in the previous year's draft were quarterbacks. Five [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_football "Georgia Bulldogs football") defensive players were taken during the first round, the most from an individual school in a draft. In addition to the high number of defensive selections, nine offensive linemen were taken in the first round, the most since [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NFL_draft "2013 NFL draft"). Conversely, only one quarterback was selected in the first round at 20th overall, the lowest for a draft's first quarterback since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_NFL_draft "1997 NFL draft"), and no running backs were taken in the first round for the first time since [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NFL_draft "2014 NFL draft").

A record nine draft-day trades with first-round picks were made, which resulted in less than half of the first-round selections being made by the teams that initially owned them. Analysts attributed the high number of trades to eight teams entering the draft without a first-round selection and a general absence of highly touted prospects.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-1)

## Host city

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city")]

Las Vegas was originally scheduled to host the [2020 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft "2020 NFL draft"), coinciding with the [Oakland Raiders' relocation to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders_relocation_to_Las_Vegas "Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas"). Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") the draft was held as a [virtual event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_event "Virtual event"). Las Vegas was given the 2022 Draft as a result.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-2)

Draft activities were held around two main locations on the Las Vegas Strip; invited players walked a floating [red carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_carpet "Red carpet") on the man-made lake in front of the [Bellagio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_(resort) "Bellagio (resort)") and its [fountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountains_of_Bellagio "Fountains of Bellagio"). The plans were similar to those originally intended for the 2020 draft, although a plan for players to be transported onto the stage by boat was scrapped in favor of using walkways.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)

Caesars Forum housed infrastructure for the event.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)[The Linq Promenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Linq_Promenade "The Linq Promenade") hosted the NFL Draft Experience, which featured fan activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4) Parts of [Flamingo Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo_Road_(Las_Vegas) "Flamingo Road (Las Vegas)") and [Las Vegas Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Boulevard "Las Vegas Boulevard") were closed to vehicle traffic to allow spectators to travel between the two sites.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

Walker is a big, rugged run-stopper with the playing style and body type to play as an even- or odd-front end. He consistently outreaches blockers to take control at the point of attack and sets firm edges despite playing with limited knee bend. He has quick-shed ability to make plays near his gaps and could see an increase in production if allowed to play in a scheme that asks more of him than Georgia did from a playmaking perspective. He has the strength and length to plow through overmatched pass protectors but will need to improve his skill level to consistently find the quarterback as a pro. Walker's blend of explosiveness and aggression could help push his draft stock beyond his tape grade.

### PROSPECT ANALYSIS

Defensive end prospect with a can't-miss combination of football character, skill and physical traits who is more likely to contend for occasional Pro Bowls than become an All-Pro playmaker. Hutchinson's strength and flexion allows him to drop a deep anchor and set a very firm edge, and that is unlikely to change as a pro whether he's used in 4-3 or 3-4 fronts. He can be too mechanical, engaging in cursory contact rather than using his hands to whip the man in front of him quickly. Hutchinson is an instinctive rusher, assailing the pocket with a non-stop barrage of activity. His hands are skilled and efficient to grease the edge while fluid counter steps open inside paths to the pocket. He needs to add a few more items to his rush menu in order to maintain his rush production against NFL tackles. Hutchinson is scheme versatile and should be a very good starter with a very high floor, but his ceiling might not be as elevated as some of the talent he's been compared to.

### PROSPECT ANALYSIS

Walker is a big, rugged run-stopper with the playing style and body type to play as an even- or odd-front end. He consistently outreaches blockers to take control at the point of attack and sets firm edges despite playing with limited knee bend. He has quick-shed ability to make plays near his gaps and could see an increase in production if allowed to play in a scheme that asks more of him than Georgia did from a playmaking perspective. He has the strength and length to plow through overmatched pass protectors but will need to improve his skill level to consistently find the quarterback as a pro. Walker's blend of explosiveness and aggression could help push his draft stock beyond his tape grade.

While Green has some areas to improve, his run blocking can be dominant, which gives him a chance to become a good starter very quickly.

## Pre-Draft Analysis

Walker is an EDGE defender with an excellent combination of height, bulk, length and straight-line speed. His pass rush is built on strength and explosion. If he can develop smoother counter moves and unlock his potential as a pass-rusher, he'll improve his sack numbers. Walker's versatility makes him an excellent fit for first-year coordinator Mike Caldwell's multiple front defense. His upside as a pass-rusher should give the Jaguars' rush a much-needed boost. His ability to line up anywhere along the defensive front and drop on passing downs will make it easier for Caldwell to mask from where he's bringing pressure and who is dropping into coverage. It'll also help Caldwell create favorable pass rush matchups. The **2022 NFL draft** was the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League")'s 87th annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_draft "NFL draft") and was held from April 28–30, 2022, at the [Caesars Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Forum "Caesars Forum") on the [Las Vegas Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Strip "Las Vegas Strip") in [Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada") next to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). The first round was held on Thursday, April 28, and was followed by the second and third rounds on Friday, April 29. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on Saturday, April 30. It was the first draft to be held in the [Las Vegas metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_metropolitan_area "Las Vegas metropolitan area") and the state of [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada").

The first five selections were defensive players, the second-most taken at the start of a draft after the six in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_NFL_draft "1991 NFL draft"). Along with the [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_NFL_draft "1972 NFL draft") and [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_NFL_draft "2000 NFL draft") drafts, it marked the third time defensive players were the first two picks after the first three picks in the previous year's draft were quarterbacks. Five [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_football "Georgia Bulldogs football") defensive players were taken during the first round, the most from an individual school in a draft. In addition to the high number of defensive selections, nine offensive linemen were taken in the first round, the most since [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NFL_draft "2013 NFL draft"). Conversely, only one quarterback was selected in the first round at 20th overall, the lowest for a draft's first quarterback since [1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_NFL_draft "1997 NFL draft"), and no running backs were taken in the first round for the first time since [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NFL_draft "2014 NFL draft").

A record nine draft-day trades with first-round picks were made, which resulted in less than half of the first-round selections being made by the teams that initially owned them. Analysts attributed the high number of trades to eight teams entering the draft without a first-round selection and a general absence of highly touted prospects.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-1)

## Host city

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city")]

Las Vegas was originally scheduled to host the [2020 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft "2020 NFL draft"), coinciding with the [Oakland Raiders' relocation to the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders_relocation_to_Las_Vegas "Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas"). Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") the draft was held as a [virtual event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_event "Virtual event"). Las Vegas was given the 2022 Draft as a result.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-2)

Draft activities were held around two main locations on the Las Vegas Strip; invited players walked a floating [red carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_carpet "Red carpet") on the man-made lake in front of the [Bellagio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_(resort) "Bellagio (resort)") and its [fountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountains_of_Bellagio "Fountains of Bellagio"). The plans were similar to those originally intended for the 2020 draft, although a plan for players to be transported onto the stage by boat was scrapped in favor of using walkways.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)

Caesars Forum housed infrastructure for the event.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4)[The Linq Promenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Linq_Promenade "The Linq Promenade") hosted the NFL Draft Experience, which featured fan activities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-:1-4) Parts of [Flamingo Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo_Road_(Las_Vegas) "Flamingo Road (Las Vegas)") and [Las Vegas Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Boulevard "Las Vegas Boulevard") were closed to vehicle traffic to allow spectators to travel between the two sites.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

steps.text:
**Answer:**  
The **NFC East** drafted the most SEC players—**three** of them—from teams that had won a Super Bowl in the 1980s.

**Why?**  
- The only 2022 draft picks from SEC schools that came from Super Bowl‑winning franchises of the 1980s are:
  1. **Jordan Davis** (Georgia) – Philadelphia Eagles (1986 Super Bowl champion) – NFC East  
  2. **Evan Neal** (Alabama) – New York Giants (1986 Super Bowl champion) – NFC East  
  3. **Cor’Dale Flott** (LSU) – New York Giants (1986 Super Bowl champion) – NFC East  

- The only other 1980s Super Bowl‑winning team that drafted an SEC player was the San Francisco 49ers, who selected **Tyrion Davis‑Price** (LSU) – that pick is in the **NFC West**.

Thus, the NFC East amassed **3** SEC selections, while the NFC West had **1**.  
The NFC East is therefore the division that drafted the most SEC players from those qualified teams.  

*Source:* The 2022 NFL Draft page (Wikipedia) lists the SEC draftees picked by 1980s Super Bowl‑winning teams and the division of each drafting franchise, showing 3 in the NFC East and 1 in the NFC West.
